---
title: "Money Story"
subtitle: "A data-driven exploration of 10+ years of personal spending"
---

## What Is This?

Money Story is a portfolio project that transforms a decade of personal financial data into
an interactive data story. It explores how spending patterns evolve alongside life events —
career changes, relocations, and the slow creep of lifestyle inflation.

## Two Ways to Explore

### Static Story

Pre-rendered narrative pages with charts that highlight key insights:

- **[Lifestyle Creep](story/lifestyle-creep.qmd)** — How total spending grows over time,
  which categories drive it, and the role of life events.
- **[Job Changes & Income](story/job-changes.qmd)** — How income transitions affect
  spending behavior and category mix.

### Interactive Exploration

In-browser tools powered by [DuckDB-Wasm](https://duckdb.org/docs/api/wasm/overview) —
no backend server, all computation happens locally:

- **[Categories Over Time](explore/categories-over-time.qmd)** — Multi-series time chart
  with zoom, toggle, and filtering.
- **[Sankey Diagram](explore/sankey.qmd)** — Income flow visualization for any date range.
- **[SQL Playground](explore/sql-playground.qmd)** — Run SQL queries against the public dataset.

## Data & Privacy

All public data is **monthly aggregates** — no individual transactions, no merchant names,
no exact timestamps. The source data is private and never committed to this repository.

**Public tables:**

| Table | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `spend_monthly_category.parquet` | Monthly spending by category (L1 + L2) |
| `income_monthly.parquet` | Monthly income totals |
| `events_public.parquet` | Life event labels and date ranges |

## Methodology

- Expenses are categorized into a two-level hierarchy (10 L1 categories, ~28 L2 subcategories).
- Income is post-tax take-home pay.
- All amounts are nominal (not inflation-adjusted).
- Charts use 6-month rolling averages to smooth seasonal variation.

## Technology

Built with [Quarto](https://quarto.org), [Plotly](https://plotly.com/python/),
[Polars](https://pola.rs), and [DuckDB-Wasm](https://duckdb.org/docs/api/wasm/overview).
Hosted on GitHub Pages with automated CI/CD.
